title: Each kb copy a test makes hard-links every file the test does not write
goal: conftest's KbTemplate.copy_to hard-links every tracked file of the per-session template that no test writes, not only _snapshots, artifacts and _census, so a kb copy costs links rather than about 60% of its bytes copied (781 of 1915 files linked today); the write-through guard still fails a test that writes a linked file; measured before and after on this host. Found by the SP-w3xmbdra review (ST-ykvho3zp's goal clause 'hard links of one per-session template' is only partly delivered).

gates.question: Linking every file a test does not write needs the list of files tests write in place: a write through a hard link changes the shared template. How is that list made? audit = one full run with every file linked, the guard naming each file written in place, those paths kept as a committed COPY list in conftest; declare = link every file and fix each failing test with copy= over several runs; narrow = link only kb/public/** articles and data, keep the rest copied, and measure

notes: Audit done 2026-10-05 (worker1): 14 paths written in place (conftest.WRITTEN); the change is committed, not landed, on worker1's local branch work/ST-b3bbbbpc (81c582c93). Not landed: a copy now copies 14 files (4.8 MB) instead of 1108 (22.9 MB) but takes about 430 ms against 327 ms on this host, so linking is slower here; the operator decides whether to land it, narrow it or drop it.
